title: Additivity of the coefficient-to-polynomial map
statement: Fix a field $K$ and natural numbers $n$ and $D$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ be the set of subsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. For a coefficient function $c \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, write $P(c) = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{n,D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s} X_i$ for the associated squarefree polynomial in $K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$. Then for any two coefficient functions $c_1, c_2 \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$ one has \[ P(c_1 + c_2) = P(c_1) + P(c_2), \] where $c_1 + c_2$ denotes the pointwise sum.
hypotheses_covered: c₁, c₂ are coefficient functions on low-degree squarefree supports S_{n,D}
replaced:
The constructor $\texttt{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}$ is additive in its coefficient
argument: the polynomial attached to $c_1 + c_2$ is the sum of the polynomials attached
to $c_1$ and to $c_2$.
